Chronology 8 — Muhammad and the Seal of Prophethood

The storyline now reaches the claim that closes it on the Islamic side: Muhammad as the final prophet, allegedly foretold in the Bible.

The Qur'an's text

  • Muhammad is "the seal of the prophets" (Q 33:40).
  • He is said to be found "written with them in the Torah and the Gospel" (Q 7:157), and Jesus foretells a messenger "whose name is Ahmad" (Q 61:6).

The alleged biblical foreshadowings (Muslim reading)

  1. Deut 18:15–18 — "a prophet like Moses from among their brethren" → read as the Ishmaelite/Arab line.
  2. John 14:16,26; 15:26; 16:7 — the Paraclete → read as Ahmad (the paraklētos → periklytos "praised one" theory).
  3. *Deut 33:2 (Paran); Isa 29:12 ("he is not learned"); Song 5:16 (maḥamaddim); Hag 2:7* — assorted prooftexts.

The Christian / academic response

  • Deut 18 "brethren": in Deuteronomy's own usage "brethren" = fellow Israelites; and the NT applies "the prophet like Moses" to Jesus (Acts 3:22). The reading is grammatically possible but contextually weaker.
  • The Paraclete: the Greek is paraklētos ("Advocate/Comforter"), and the text self-identifies it as the Holy Spirit who would come soon and dwell in the disciples (John 14:17,26) — not a future Arabian prophet. The periklytos ("Ahmad") emendation has no manuscript support whatsoever — and by the dossier's own manuscript standard (cap. 02, cap. 06), a reading with zero manuscript attestation cannot be asserted as the text.
  • The remaining prooftexts rest on isolated words read out of context.

Arbiter verdict — Muhammad foretold?

Present. Islam: Muhammad is the foretold, final prophet. Christianity/ academy: the cited texts refer to Israelite prophecy, Jesus, or the Holy Spirit, and the periklytos theory is text-critically baseless.

Weigh.

  • As historical/textual claims: weak. The Paraclete-as-Ahmad reading has no manuscript basis (the very standard the dossier applied to the Comma Johanneum, applied evenly here); the Deut 18 reading is contextually disfavoured.
  • As faith claims: non-falsifiable. "These passages secretly point to Muhammad" cannot be disproved, but neither can it be evidenced — and unfalsifiable is not the same as supported (Methodology §1.4, §4).
  • Finality / "seal": a theological axiom, not a historical datum; it has no pre-Islamic documentary footprint.

Judge. On the textual/historical question — do the biblical texts foretell Muhammad? — the evidence is weak to negative, decisively so for the Paraclete claim by the dossier's own evenly-applied manuscript rule. On the theological claim of finality, the arbiter does not rule true or false (out of remit) but does record that it rests on doctrine, not on documentary evidence. Symmetry holds: the same scalpel that cut the Christian Comma Johanneum cuts the Muslim periklytos reading.
